summary: Closes FIND-M9-72-SANDBOX-SHARED-STORE-SAVE-TIMEOUT, the deferral m9-72 recorded when it found its required T4-smoke subset flaky. The finding said the sandbox harness shares one store and proposed giving each client a unique CHRONOS_DB_PATH. Recon found three independent writers of that variable, not one: McpTestClient::start/start_path spawned the server with the caller's environment so every client resolved the developer's $HOME store, session_edge_cases' SE1 called std::env::set_var around two start() calls (mutating the environment of the whole test binary, so other tests on other threads inherited it), and ce12 called set_var 'so the CLI replay can find the same store' - untrue, because replay_bundle passes --db <path> explicitly. start_path now allocates a private store (PID + atomic counter + nanos) and passes CHRONOS_DB_PATH through start_with_env; the field is removed on Drop after the child is reaped; start_with_db_path stays as the explicit opt-in for sharing; the spawn helper no longer inherits an ambient CHRONOS_DB_PATH at all; both global-mutation sites are gone - which also let SE1 be un-ignored, since the interference its #[ignore] guarded against was exactly that mutation. A new CC#56 forbids std::env::set_var/remove_var anywhere in chronos-sandbox so the class cannot return, and a new suite asserts store isolation against what the server actually opened on disk rather than what the client recorded. Running the required subset also surfaced a pre-existing failure unrelated to the cycle: session_edge_cases has two tests whose session_save never completes in this environment, on main as well (measured by interleaved A/B, and it still fails with a 180 s timeout), now recorded in AGENTS.md 6.5.
title: 73 sandbox client store isolation

subject.gap: The sandbox T4-smoke subset was flaky: session_persistence::test_save_session_multiple_times failed with TimeoutError("method=tools/call", 30s) at session_persistence.rs:128 or :133 in a subset of runs, on main as well as on the cycle branch, and the failing runs were the slow ones (76-80 s of suite wall time vs 55-64 s). Mechanism: McpTestClient::start() -> start_path() -> factory::start() spawned the server with the caller's environment, so every sandbox client resolved default_db_path() = $HOME/.local/share/chronos/sessions.redb, one 86 MB store shared by all 35 suites, and session_save serializes ~2500 compressed events into it behind a fixed 30 s client timeout. Two further writers of the same variable were hiding behind the first: session_edge_cases::test_load_session_persists_across_client_instances set it globally (remove_var, set_var, set_var again, remove_var) and counterexample_tools::ce12 set it under a comment claiming the CLI replay needed it, which is not true - replay_bundle passes --db <path> explicitly. The class was invisible because a shared store usually works: it fails only when one process writes a large session while another holds the database, which is a timing accident rather than an assertion.
subject.fix: chronos-sandbox/src/client/tools.rs: McpTestClient gains db_dir/db_path; start_path allocates a private temp store via allocate_store_dir() (unique by PID + process-local atomic counter + nanosecond timestamp), starts the server with it via a new db_env() helper, and removes the directory in a new Drop impl that takes the process handle first so the child is reaped before its store is deleted; start() delegates to start_path() through a new resolve_mcp_path() (the binary-resolution ladder was duplicated in start and start_with_db_path); start_with_db_path keeps the explicit-shared-store behaviour, drops the redundant std::env::vars() base, and records db_dir: None so the caller's path is never deleted. chronos-sandbox/src/client/process.rs::spawn_with_env now removes CHRONOS_DB_PATH before applying extra_env, so the child's store is only ever what the caller passed (Command inherits the parent environment by default, which is how the ambient value leaked). session_edge_cases SE1 and counterexample_tools ce12 no longer touch the process environment. New tests/client_store_isolation.rs (3 tests) asserts isolation by observing the filesystem: the store file the client recorded must exist and be non-empty (open_default_store silently falls back to an in-memory store, so file presence is what proves the server opened it), two clients must differ, and the value must not be the ambient default. New CC#56 (python) walks chronos-sandbox for std::env::(set_var|remove_var).

deferred.note: ContentStore::put (crates/chronos-store/src/cas.rs:55) opens a redb write transaction per event, calls ensure_table on it, inserts one row, and commits; no set_durability call exists anywhere in the crate, so redb's default immediate durability makes each commit a durability barrier (fsync). SessionStore::save_session (storage.rs:158) calls cas.put in a loop over the session's events before opening its own metadata transaction, so saving one session costs one fsync per event. How it surfaced: session_edge_cases::test_compare_sessions_crash_vs_normal prints 'Crash session stopped: 34905 events' and then fails to save within the client's 30 s tools/call timeout; raising the timeout to 180 s still fails after 186 s. The numbers are consistent to within measurement error with a linear per-event cost of roughly 4.8 ms (34,905 events x 4.8 ms = 168 s, against >186 s observed), which is also the right order for a 2,500-event save taking a few seconds - the volume session_persistence uses, and why that suite sits just under a 30 s client timeout when nothing contends. Consequences: any session above roughly 6,000 events approaches the 30 s sandbox client timeout, and realistic sessions (a crash capture is 35k events here) take minutes. This is a product-facing cost, not just a test one: the MCP client timeout is what makes it a hard failure, but a three-minute session_save is a usability defect regardless. Proposed fix, not attempted in this cycle: add ContentStore::put_many(&[TraceEvent]) that opens one write transaction and inserts every event in it (the dedup check per event stays, the transaction moves out of the loop), and have save_session batch its events through it; keep put as the single-event convenience wrapper over put_many. Verify by saving a 35k-event session and asserting wall time.
deferred.severity_rationale: Linear fsync-per-event write path: a single crash session (35k events) does not complete in three minutes, and the cost is on the save path of every session, not just tests.

deferred.note: Falsification of this cycle's own tests exposed a defect one layer below them: crates/chronos-mcp/src/server.rs::open_default_store falls back to SessionStore::in_memory() when the configured store cannot be opened (locked, corrupt, missing parent), logging only a tracing::warn. A server that is asked to open the developer's or a test's store while another process holds it therefore starts successfully with an empty in-memory store: session_save reports success and session_list returns 0 sessions, i.e. silent data loss with a green health check, instead of an error. This is exactly what the pre-m9-73 shared store did to the second sandbox client, and it is why the first version of the isolation test passed with the guard removed: client B saw 0 sessions and the assertion 'B must not see A's session' was satisfied by the fallback rather than by isolation. Not fixed here - the fallback is a deliberate resilience choice (it keeps the server usable when the local store is locked, and SessionStore::in_memory() has its own uses), the correct remedy is a policy decision (fail closed on a store that exists but cannot be opened, keep the fallback only for a missing parent directory, or surface the degraded mode in a tool response), and it belongs to chronos-mcp rather than to the sandbox harness. Detection is now in place: the isolation suite fails if it ever runs against a fallback store again.
deferred.severity_rationale: Silent data loss, but requires a store that exists and is locked or unreadable, which in practice means two processes against one configured path.

deferred.note: Two tests in chronos-sandbox/tests/session_edge_cases.rs fail on every observed run in this environment, on the cycle branch and on main alike: test_compare_sessions_crash_vs_normal and test_performance_regression_audit_different_workloads, both with save_session failed: TimeoutError("method=tools/call", 30s). The suite was red when the cycle first ran it, so attribution was measured rather than assumed. Interleaved A/B with alternating builds, three rounds each, whole suite, --test-threads=1: cycle branch 3/2/2 failures, main 2/2/2 failures; the same two tests fail on both sides every round (line numbers differ by exactly the eight lines this cycle removed from the top of the file). The failure is not a calibration problem: the save is retried with the client RPC timeout raised to 180 s and still fails, after 186 s, with TimeoutError("method=tools/call", 180s) - so session_save on a crash/segfault probe session genuinely does not complete rather than merely being slow. This cycle did not cause it: its diff touches client store allocation (tools.rs, process.rs) and two test bodies (SE1's store wiring and ce12's redundant env mutation), none of which the failing tests execute; SE1 itself passes 2/2 when run, and was therefore un-ignored. Recorded in AGENTS.md 6.5 so future cycles do not chase it as a regression. Next investigation should start from the event volume of the crash session (the test prints 'Crash session stopped: N events' before saving) and from whether probe_drain leaves the capture in a state session_save cannot compress.
deferred.severity_rationale: Bucket C red on two tests in every run, on main too; no product impact observed, but it makes this suite unable to signal regressions.

deferred.note: CC#4 requires that after editing cycles/index.md, terms/index.md or any file listed in an archive manifest's artifact index, the SHA rows of every prior archive manifest that lists them are regenerated, and the loop must be run to a fixpoint. That regeneration is done by a throwaway python script that lives in the agent's scratch directory, not in the repository, so every cycle re-derives it (this cycle did, and so did m9-72). Two footguns follow. First, a whole-tree run rewrites the self-referential 'archive-manifest (this file)' row of every manifest, including nine pre-m9-11 manifests (m9-01, m9-03..m9-10) that are never in the affected set; those rows are unmaintainable by construction (a file cannot contain its own hash) and CC#4 skips them by design, so the rewrite is pure unrelated churn - this cycle reverted it and restored m9-67/m9-68's self rows to their committed values, leaving only the two rows CC#4 actually requires. Second, a script that follows the naive 'recompute every row' rule is what produced the m9-02 self-row defect that m9-72 had to zero. Remedy: land scripts/regen_manifest_index_shas.py with the skip-self-row rule and document it in maintenance/vault-drift-sweep.md next to CC#4. Not done here to keep a test-harness cycle from growing a tooling surface, and because the affected set (which grows by one manifest every cycle, FIND-M9-71-ARCHIVE-MANIFEST-INDEX-SHA-CHAINTENSION) makes the script worth writing deliberately rather than in passing.
